scenes.title: Linear Delta Model vs. Quadratic Delta-Gamma Model

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Linear Delta Model: $\Delta P = \sum \delta_i \Delta S_i$, computationally fast but ignores non-linear option curvature ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Quadratic Delta-Gamma Model: incorporates second-order Gamma term $ rac{1}{2}\Gamma(\Delta S)^2$ to prevent catastrophic option risk underestimation ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down EWMA Formula: $\sigma_n^2 = \lambda \sigma_{n-1}^2 + (1-\lambda) u_{n-1}^2$ using decay factor $\lambda = 0.94$ for daily data ([fact-06]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down GARCH(1,1) Formula: $\sigma_n^2 = \omega + \alpha u_{n-1}^2 +  eta \sigma_{n-1}^2$ incorporating mean reversion toward long-run variance $V_L$ ([fact-07]).

scenes.title: GARCH(1,1) Volatility Term Structure Mean Reversion

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine Elevated Volatility: when current volatility exceeds long-run average $V_L$, the term structure is downward-sloping ([fact-08]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine Depressed Volatility: when current volatility is below $V_L$, expected future variance reverts upward, creating an upward-sloping term structure ([fact-08]).

summarySteps: 1. Model-Building Approach ([fact-01]): Calculates parametric portfolio risk assuming multivariate normal asset returns via $\sigma_P^2 = w^T \Sigma w$.
2. Diversification Benefit ([fact-05]): Combining Microsoft and AT&T reduces total 99% VaR to $496,600 compared to the $581,500 sum of individual VaRs.
3. Linear Delta Model ([fact-03]): Approximates derivatives value changes using Delta, but ignores option curvature.
4. Quadratic Delta-Gamma Model ([fact-04]): Incorporates second-order Taylor series expansions to capture convex option curvature.
5. EWMA Model ([fact-06]): Updates variance recursively with exponential decay ($\lambda = 0.94$) giving more weight to recent market shocks.
6. GARCH(1,1) Model ([fact-07], [fact-08]): Incorporates mean reversion toward long-run variance $V_L$, determining upward or downward volatility term structures.
7. Kupiec POF Test ([fact-09]): Statistically validates VaR model exception rates against theoretical failure probabilities.
8. LTCM Collapse ([fact-10]): 1998 market panic caused historical correlations to surge toward 1.0, invalidating normal distribution assumptions.
bottomTakeaway: The model-building approach enables rapid parametric VaR and covariance calculations, which must be augmented with quadratic Delta-Gamma approximations and EWMA/GARCH volatility updating to withstand market panics like LTCM ([fact-01], [fact-04], [fact-06], [fact-10]).
